description: Generate files from docker container meta-data

summary.one_liner: docker-gen is a command-line file generator that renders Go text/templates using Docker container metadata, commonly used to build reverse proxy configs, logging configs, and service discovery files.
summary.what_it_does: "Renders templates using metadata from running Docker containers, such as IDs, names, networks, addresses, ports, labels, environment variables, volumes, and health state. It can run once and write to a file or stdout, or use -watch to regenerate output when container start, stop, die, or health_status events occur. After regenerating, it can run a shell command (-notify) or send a signal such as HUP to containers (-notify-sighup, -notify-container, -notify-filter). Containers can be filtered with -container-filter, -only-exposed, -only-published, or -include-stopped. The README documents a large set of template helpers, including grouping, filtering, sorting, YAML and JSON conversion, and nginx-specific quoting and HSTS validation. Configuration can also be supplied through an INI-style config file with multiple templates."
use_cases: generate nginx reverse proxy config from running containers
regenerate config and reload nginx when containers change
produce fluentd or logstash config from container logs
generate logrotate config for container JSON logs
register containers in etcd via generated script
run docker-gen in a separate container alongside nginx
how_to_run: Download a docker-gen release binary, extract it, and place it on your PATH

docker run -d --name nginx-gen --volumes-from nginx -v /var/run/docker.sock:/tmp/docker.sock:rw -v /tmp/templates:/etc/docker-gen/templates -t nginxproxy/docker-gen -notify-sighup nginx -watch -only-exposed /etc/docker-gen/templates/nginx.tmpl /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf
notable: Runs as a host binary, bundled inside another container, or as a standalone companion container sharing volumes with the target service
Template helpers for grouping, filtering, and sorting containers by labels or nested fields (groupBy, whereLabelExists, sortObjectsByKeysAsc)
Deterministic ordering of Addresses and Networks so output stays stable across regenerations
Config file mode supports multiple templates executed in order and per-template notify container settings
Maintained by ZeroSSL according to the README
caveats: Requires access to the Docker socket or API endpoint, which is a privilege concern if exposed to other containers
Development build requires Go 1.26 or newer
Template authoring requires knowledge of Go text/template syntax and the emitted struct layout
